singlePurpose.title: Single Purpose Declaration
singlePurpose.description: ZFocus is a productivity tool designed to help users manage their time by limiting access to distracting websites. This is its sole purpose.

dataCollection.title: Data Collection
dataCollection.noData: ZFocus does NOT collect any personal data.
dataCollection.description: We believe in complete privacy. Here's what that means:

items.noBrowsingHistory: No browsing history is collected or transmitted
items.noAnalytics: No usage analytics are sent to external servers
items.noTracking: No third-party tracking scripts are included
items.noDataSold: No data is sold or shared with anyone

dataStorage.title: Data Storage
dataStorage.description: ZFocus stores the following data locally on your device:

settings.title: Settings (chrome.storage.sync)
settings.description: Your blocked website lists, time limits, schedules, and preferences. This data can optionally sync across your Chrome browsers if you're signed into Chrome.

statistics.title: Statistics (chrome.storage.local)
statistics.description: Daily statistics including blocked attempt counts and time paused. Historical stats are kept for 30 days. This data stays on your local device only.

timerData.title: Timer Data (chrome.storage.sync)
timerData.description: Current timer states for active blocked sites.

dataStorage.noServer: All data remains on your device or within your personal Chrome sync account. No data is transmitted to ZFocus servers.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: ZFocus requires certain browser permissions to function. Each permission is used solely for the extension's core functionality:

storage.name: storage
storage.reason: To save your settings, blocked website lists, and daily statistics locally on your device.

tabs.name: tabs
tabs.reason: To monitor which websites you visit and apply blocking rules when a distracting site is detected.

alarms.name: alarms
alarms.reason: To reset hourly time limits and schedule blocking periods.

sidePanel.name: sidePanel
sidePanel.reason: To display the ZFocus side panel for quick access to focus settings and timer controls.

webNavigation.name: webNavigation
webNavigation.reason: To detect page navigation events and apply blocking rules during in-page navigations.

idle.name: idle
idle.reason: To detect when the user is idle and pause active-tab-only timers accordingly.

permissions.onlyForCore: These permissions are used solely for the extension's core functionality and nothing else.

thirdParty.title: Third-Party Services
thirdParty.noServices: ZFocus does not use any third-party analytics, tracking, or advertising services.
thirdParty.errorMonitoring: The extension includes optional, opt-in error monitoring (Sentry) to help developers fix bugs. This is disabled by default and only activated with your explicit consent. When enabled, only anonymous crash reports are sent -- no personal data, browsing history, or blocked site information is included.

dataDeletion.description: You can delete all ZFocus data at any time:
dataDeletion.uninstall: Alternatively, uninstalling the extension will remove all locally stored data.

comparison.title: Why ZFocus?
comparison.subtitle: See how ZFocus compares to other popular tools for managing screen time and reducing distractions
comparison.openSourceNote: ZFocus will be open-sourced once we reach a sustainable user base to cover development costs.

footnotes.1: LeechBlock NG has 30+ block sets with advanced options including regex, wildcards, and lockdown features. Powerful but can overwhelm new users who just want to block a few sites.
footnotes.2: LeechBlock supports exceptions via + prefix and wildcards, but requires manually writing URL patterns. ZFocus provides a visual interface to add exception rules.
footnotes.3: LeechBlock can achieve break-like behavior through time period configuration (e.g. unblock during 12:00-13:00), but has no dedicated break/lunch mode with one-click toggle.
footnotes.4: Screen Time on Safari/iOS only supports daily time limits. It does not allow setting hourly limits for gradual reduction throughout the day.
footnotes.5: LeechBlock can block specific URL paths, but requires creating separate block sets for each pattern (e.g. one for youtube.com/shorts, another for facebook.com/reel). ZFocus handles this within a single rule.
footnotes.6: LeechBlock uses a functional but dated interface. ZFocus offers a modern UI with light/dark/auto themes.
footnotes.7: LeechBlock offers basic statistics (time spent per block set). ZFocus provides 30-day visual charts with blocks, time saved, and streaks.
footnotes.8: Screen Time syncs usage data through iCloud. ZFocus and LeechBlock store everything locally with zero tracking.
footnotes.9: LeechBlock NG is fully open source. ZFocus plans to open source once it reaches a sustainable user base.
footnotes.10: ZFocus works on Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Firefox. LeechBlock supports Firefox, Chrome, and Edge. Screen Time is Safari/iOS only.
